blogs.title: The Butterfly Secret: Why Math Behind Fourier Transforms Makes Finetuning Faster
blogs.description: In this post, we demystify how the Cooley-Tukey algorithm and 'butterfly structures' from signal processing can be repurposed to train massive AI models more efficiently. We explore how utilizing these elegant patterns allows researchers to generate complex, dense updates using far fewer computational parameters than traditional methods.

blogs.title: Beyond Low-Rank Updates: The Rise of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT)
blogs.description: While LoRA has dominated parameter-efficient finetuning, a novel approach called Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) is challenging the status quo. This article explains the mathematical intuition behind OFT—preserving the geometric angles between neurons—and why it leads to more stable training and generalized models, especially for difficult tasks like high-quality image generation.

blogs.title: From Block-Diagonal to Butterfly Factorization: Solving the Parameter Efficiency Paradox
blogs.description: We dive deep into the technical bottleneck of OFT: while mathematically sound, it originally required too many parameters due to the high dimensionality of orthogonal matrices. This post analyzes how 'butterfly factorization' provides a brilliant Graph-theoretic solution, reducing parameters from $\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ to $\mathcal{O}(d \log d)$ while maintaining powerful expressivity.
